about: The evangelium of the formulary “Second Sunday after Epiphany” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, a wedding was held in Cana of Galilee, and the Mother of Jesus was there. Now Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding. And when the wine ran out, the Mother of Jesus says to Him: They have no wine. And Jesus says to her: What is that to Me and to you, Woman? My hour has not yet come. His Mother says to the servants: Do whatever He tells you. Now there were six stone waterpots set there according to the purification of the Jews, each able to hold two or three measures. Jesus says to them: Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim. And Jesus says to them: Draw some now and take it to the chief steward. And they carried it. Now when the chief steward had tasted the water made into wine and did not know where it was from—but the servants who had drawn the water knew—the chief steward calls the bridegroom and says to him: Everyone sets out good wine first, and when the guests have become drunk, then that which is worse. You, however, have kept the good wine until now. Jesus performed this, the beginning of signs, in Cana of Galilee, and manifested His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.

ex.w068: Capientes describes the capacity of the waterpots. Singulae makes the stated amount apply to each one: two or three measures per waterpot, not a combined total for all six.
ex.w130: Fuerint can be future perfect indicative or perfect subjunctive in form. With inebriati it presents a resulting state of drunkenness in the steward’s description of a general custom, not an assertion about these wedding guests. The plural drinkers are the understood subject. English “when the guests have become drunk” expresses the sequence without deciding the Latin mood.
